name: Boeing 737
headline: length
subtitle: 737-8 (737 MAX 8)
description: The Boeing 737 is a twin-engine, single-aisle airliner family; the 737 MAX series, with CFM LEAP-1B engines and dual-feather Advanced Technology winglets, is its latest generation. Boeing's airport planning document gives the 737-8 an overall length of 129 ft 6 in (39.47 m) and a wingspan of 117 ft 10 in (35.92 m). It seats 178 passengers in a typical two-class layout and can take off at up to 182,200 lb.

measures.label: Length
measures.note: 737-8 overall length, 129 ft 6 in; Boeing's drawings are accurate within +/- 6 inches

measures.label: Tail height
measures.note: Ground to top of the vertical stabilizer (38 ft 11 in to 40 ft 10 in), varying with loading, oleo and tire pressures

measures.label: Maximum takeoff weight
measures.note: 737-8 maximum design takeoff weight options (72,302 to 82,644 kg)

measures.label: Lower-deck cargo volume
measures.note: Maximum lower-deck cargo volume (42.9 cubic metres)

facts.text: The 737-8 seats 178 passengers in a two-class layout or 189 in a single class.
The 737 MAX family covers the 737-7, 737-8, 737-8-200, 737-9, 737-10 and Business Jet versions, all powered by CFM LEAP-1B engines.
The 737 MAX remains an FAA Airplane Design Group III and ICAO Aerodrome Reference Code C aircraft, the same airport category as earlier 737s.

sources.title: 737 MAX Airplane Characteristics for Airport Planning (D6-38A004, Rev K, July 2025)

caveats: All figures are for the 737-8 (737 MAX 8). Other 737 versions range from shorter (737-7) to longer (737-10), and older generations differ.
Length, wingspan and fuselage length were read from Boeing's general-dimensions drawing (section 2.2.2), which Boeing says is accurate within +/- 6 inches.
